title: Molecular Mechanisms of Myoblast Fusion
text:
Myoblast fusion is an essential step during skeletal muscle development and muscle stem cell-based
regeneration. Understanding the mechanisms of myoblast fusion will lead to significant insights into human
muscle biology in health and disease, and ultimately provide basis for developing more efficient therapeutics
against the life debilitating muscle degenerative diseases.

title: Molecular Mechanisms of Insulin Resistance Associated Loci
text:
Insulin resistance (IR) is a common and increasing health problem that precedes development of type 2
diabetes and causes cardiovascular disease, but its genetic determinants are largely unknown. We will
combine innovative methods including colocalization studies followed by single cell transcriptomics and single
cell epigenomics to establish causal genes and mechanisms of action for novel genes involved in development
of IR, and validate the physiological role of causal genes in vitro and in vivo using mouse models in a fat-depot
specific way. Our work will lead to mechanistic insights into the development of IR and to better treatments for
IR and related conditions.

title: Regulation of Hepatic Drug Transport Proteins: Identifying Novel Drug Interaction Signals
text:
Organic anion transporting polypeptides OATP1B1, OATP1B3 and organic cation transporter 1 are key liver
transporters that facilitate the uptake of numerous drugs and nutrients from the bloodstream into the liver. This
research will uncover novel regulatory mechanisms that influence the activity of these critical transport
proteins. Such information is essential for predicting clinically relevant drug-drug and drug-nutrient interactions.

title: Novel gene delivery to modulate the tumor microenvironment and antigen-specific antitumor immunity
text:
The intratumoral viral gene delivery containing a novel combination of herpes simplex
virus -thymidine kinase gene (HSV-tk) and bifunctional antibody and prolongation of the
gene expression may provide a novel and inexpensive therapeutic regimen, offering a
truly transformative approach for cancer treatment.

title: High-throughput single-cell RNA sequencing of bacteria to uncover cell states involved in pathogenesis
text:
Salmonella is an important human pathogen and estimated by the CDC to cause more foodborne diseases than
any other pathogen. Over one million estimated cases of Salmonella foodborne illnesses occur in the United
States every year, with an economic burden of approximately $3.7 billion dollars per year. We will develop a
method for measuring the molecular states of individual Salmonella cells during infection to devise new treatment
strategies against Salmonella infection.

title: The Influence of Public Health Infrastructure on Prosecutorial Responses to the Opioid Crisis
text:
As the overdose crisis continues, some local prosecutors have increased their use of criminal legal
penalties to address overdose deaths—despite evidence suggesting that doing so worsens public health
outcomes for people who use drugs and their communities. Using a legal epidemiological framework, this
study analyzes (1) the factors that influence prosecutors’ decisions to treat an overdose as a murder instead of
a public health issue, (2) how such charges impact the health of people at risk of overdose, and (3) how
investment in local public health efforts can decrease the involvement of the criminal justice system in
addressing overdose deaths.

title: Germline Transformation of Ticks
text:
Ticks are obligate hematophagous arthropods and ecto-parasites of every class of vertebrates in almost
every region of the world. Despite the increasing information available on ticks, there is lack of molecular
tools to understand the basis of tick phenotypes and tick-pathogen interactions. This proposal focus on
understanding tick biology on molecular level by developing genome editing tools.

title: Toward efficient performance for deep learning on medical imaging
text:
Medical imaging is critical to almost every type of diagnostic and management decision, but human
interpretation of medical images can lack accuracy and reproducibility. By developing machine learning
methods for analyzing medical images, the work in our proposal can continue to improve diagnostic accuracy
in medical imaging, for both clinical and research uses, by leveraging the latest machine learning tools.

title: Mechanisms underlying sex-dependent pregnancy outcomes caused by fetal and maternal genomic instability
text:
Proper replication of the genome is essential to prevent birth defects and adult diseases. This application
addresses how genomic instability during development can trigger inflammation in the placenta during mid-
gestation, leading to embryonic lethality in a manner that preferentially affects female embryos. If successful,
this project will illuminate how genomic defects can contribute to serious obstetrical syndromes.

title: NR4A1 Antagonists Inhibit Colorectal Cancer Growth and Enhance Immune Surveillance
text:
PROJECT RELEVANCE
 The orphan nuclear receptor 4A1 (NR4A1, Nur77) is overexpressed in colon cancer patients and this
receptor not only regulates genes associated with tumor cell growth, survival and invasion but also plays a
pivotal role in immune suppression and T-cell exhaustion. Bis-indole derived agents (CDIMs) developed in our
laboratories are high affinity ligands (and antagonists) of NR4A1 and their dual role as chemotherapeutic and
immunotherapeutic agents will be investigated in cell culture and mouse colon tumor models.

title: Predictive modeling of mammalian cell fate transitions over time and space with single-cell genomics
text:
Through an organic synthesis of mathematical modeling, machine learning, and single-cell genomics,
this project aims to bridges the unmet gap between the “big data” from single-cell genomics and
quantitative/predictive modeling in order to address fundamental questions in mammalian cell fate
transitions, and to provide potential avenues for regenerative medicine. In particular, I propose to 1)
dissect the mechanisms of mammalian cell differentiation, reprogramming, and maintenance through
differentiable deep learning frameworks; 2) integrate multi-omics and harmonize short-term RNA
velocities with long-term lineage tracing; and 3) build predictive in silico 3D spatiotemporal models of
organogenesis.

title: Reducing infections and blockage associated with long-term implantation of ventriculoperitoneal and related shunts
text:
Project Narrative for Public Release:
Ventricular shunts (VS) are put in place by surgeons for patients with hydrocephalus to
drain the elevated pressure of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) in the brain. Current products
fail to reduce the high incidence of deadly infections or blockage of shunt drainage
tubing. Patented, second generation WynnVision ventricular shunts hold promise for
mitigating these life-threatening adverse events by way of proposed R&D including
NAMSA, Wayne State University, and the VCU Department of Neurosurgery to prepare
for FDA approval and manufacturing in a GMP facility.

title: Developing Interpretable Hematology Deep Learning Models For Linking Morphology To Molecular Features In Multiple Myeloma
text:
Multiple myeloma is a blood cancer characterized by highly variable treatment responses, making optimal
therapy selection challenging for physicians and patients. While molecular testing can help predict disease
behavior, these specialized tests are often inaccessible due to cost and logistics. We propose that routine bone
marrow tissue samples contain valuable prognostic information that can be systematically analyzed using deep
learning methods, ultimately providing accessible tools to support personalized treatment decisions in multiple
myeloma care.

title: A Multimodal and Progressive Data Science Training Program to Strengthen the Addiction Research Workforce
text: The proposed program addresses a significant gap by developing and implementing a novel model to train undergraduate and graduate students in Mississippi in applying data science methods for addiction research. It creates a progressive pathway to facilitate learning access. It begins by using a series of webinars to engage campus-wide audiences to raise awareness and interest, then provides students with hands-on training and mentored research experiences, while aiming to integrate content into course curricula for long-term sustainability.

title: Core D: Neuropath Core
text: Summary/Abstract Neuropathology Core (NC) The Neuropathology Core (NC) at the Boston University Alzheimer’s Disease Research Center (BU ADRC) is a nationally recognized leader in advancing the understanding of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and Alzheimer’s disease-related disorders (ADRD), with particular expertise in the consequences of traumatic brain injury (TBI) and repetitive head impacts (RHI). The Core’s research has established critical links between RHI and the development of multiple, often comorbid neuropathologies—including chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE), increased beta-amyloid plaques, cerebral amyloid angiopathy (CAA), Lewy body disease, TDP-43 proteinopathy, vascular pathologies, white matter rarefaction, and sulcal-specific neurodegeneration. Leveraging cutting-edge digital pathology, machine learning, and rigorous tissue banking, the NC provides state-of-the-art diagnostic evaluations, harmonized data distribution, and deep phenotyping integrated with molecular, clinical, and exposome data. The Core employs digital whole slide imaging and clearly defined machine learning (ML) pipelines to extract and quantify pathologic, vascular, inflammatory, and white matter features from brain tissue specimens. These digital pathology metrics are systematically integrated with clinical, exposome, omics, and digital cognitive phenotyping data, enabling the identification of disease subtypes and trajectories that are central to the BU ADRC mission. Importantly, reproducible computational tools such as SuStaIn are deployed, and efforts are closely coordinated with the DMS and GMP Cores to ensure alignment and maximize the utility of digital pathology and omic datasets. Advanced ex vivo imaging is also incorporated into the Core’s diagnostic workflow, utilizing high-resolution structural scans—such as T2 and FLAIR MRI. These ex vivo images are co-registered with histopathology, digital slides, and previously acquired in vivo MRI scans, supporting multi-modal spatial analyses of neurodegeneration. Ex vivo imaging enhances the precise localization and characterization of pathological changes within brain architecture and strengthens the ability to link imaging biomarkers to histological and molecular findings. The NC is deeply committed to training and mentorship, offering interdisciplinary education in modern neuropathology, digital and computational pathology, and multi-omics, thereby empowering the next generation of dementia researchers. By coordinating robust scientific resources, deploying reproducible analytic tools, and fostering collaborative research, the Neuropathology Core drives transformative progress in understanding, detecting, and treating AD/ADRD, with focused attention on populations at elevated risk due to head trauma.

title: Characterization of Longitudinal EEG Biomarkers in Chronic Low Back Pain
text:
Prognostic biomarkers support precision-based treatments yet are lacking for patients with chronic lower back
pain. Here, I aim to use advanced electroencephalogram-based neuroimaging strategies to identify and
characterize biomarkers of dysfunctional brain networks (resting-state, cognitive, and emotional) in patients
with chronic low back pain across time. The information gained from this study will increase our understanding
of the neural processes underlying chronic pain and inform future patient-oriented research and solutions.

title: 1/5 Clinical Outcome Prediction of Psychosis from EHRs (COPPER)
text:
Precision Medicine has now been firmly incorporated into the routine standard-of-care in many medical
specialties, in stark contrast with Psychiatry where quantitative predictors that guide clinical decision-making
remain extremely limited. Our proposed studies aim to advance the goals of Precision Psychiatry by using
artificial intelligence to build clinical outcome predictors of psychosis through integration of electronic health
records, dimensional phenotyping, and genetic information, in addition to exploring the psychosocial impact on
patients and clinicians. Our long-term goal is to advance the tools available for personalized approaches to
diagnosis, treatment, and prognosis in mental health.

title: In Situ Skin Regeneration through Induction of Skin Allograft Chimerism for Treatment of Severe Burn Wounds
text:
A breakthrough to achieve regeneration of perfect skin has become a major aim in wound healing especially for
large burns. The goal of this proposal is to understand the mechanisms of skin regeneration through repopulation
of skin allografts in small animal models and to demonstrate the efficacy and feasibility of our novel stem cell
mobilizing therapy in repopulation of skin allografts in a preclinical large animal (swine) model of full thickness
burns. The translational outcome of this proposal will be a simple, safe and clinically pertinent protocol using
FDA approved drugs to induce skin regeneration and to improve the treatment of victims of severe burns.

title: Elucidating mechanisms of PARP inhibitor resistance in IDH-mutant cancers
text:
Targeted therapy agents like inhibitors of poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP), which target cancers that have
DNA repair defects, have been shown to be effective in tumors such as those harboring isocitrate dehydrogenase
(IDH) mutations. Nonetheless, drug resistance continues to be a barrier in cancer therapy, mostly in part due to
heterogeneity within tumors. This project studies mechanisms of PARP inhibitor resistance in IDH-mutant
cancers, laying the foundation to define treatments for IDH-mutant cancers that are effective and personalized.

title: TR&D Project 3: OpenSim for Prediction
text: Physiologically accurate models of the musculoskeletal system coupled with physics-based simulation allow researchers to analyze human movement and understand the effects of interventions. OpenSim is used by labs around the world to model and simulate the musculoskeletal system. OpenSim’s biomechanics models encapsulate decades of experimental measurements, and the software has been tested by thousands of researchers. OpenSim has been used to uncover the contributors to gait disorders in children with cerebral palsy, create personalized gait modification strategies to reduce pain of osteoarthritis, design exoskeleton assistance strategies, and in hundreds of other applications. Through OpenSim’s open-source libraries, graphical user interface, application programming interface, and scripting interfaces, users with a broad range of interests and skills have access to state-of-the-art musculoskeletal simulation. Our aims for advancing OpenSim include the following: 1. Create tools for muscle-driven simulation in OpenSim that reduce computation time by 100X. We will incorporate automatic differentiation and polynomial-based models of muscle geometry to reduce the time to create simulations by two orders of magnitude. This performance optimization will enable our CPs to perform the large-scale simulation studies needed for their research. 2. Synthesize movement data to augment the datasets needed to train machine learning models. We will create a platform in OpenSim to rapidly generate synthetic movement data using musculoskeletal simulation. Synthetic data will be used to increase samples of underrepresented movement tasks in the AddBiomechanics dataset and augment datasets of individuals walking with exoskeletons and powered prostheses for predictive machine learning models 3. Combine machine learning with musculoskeletal simulation to predict personalized response to assistance from exoskeletons and powered prostheses. We will build on our preliminary work using a deep machine learning model to create “digital twins” that accurately predict changes in kinematics, kinetics, and muscle forces when wearing an assistive device. Our fast simulator will directly benefit the many users of OpenSim and also allow us to rapidly create synthetic human movement data to train machine learning models. By augmenting experimental data with synthetic data, we will produce sufficient training data to develop machine learning models that accurately encapsulate how humans adapt to wearing an exoskeleton, which will support a paradigm shift in the field. The digital twins we create of exoskeleton and prosthesis users will be employed by our Collaborative Projects to create novel adaptive exosuits and prosthetics for amputees and stroke survivors. Our predictive simulations will provide the breakthrough needed to support people with mobility limitations.
